Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with ongoing right knee pain, swelling, and reduced range of
motion. Over the course of 29 visits, care consisted of physical therapy, activity modification, anti-inflammatory medication, and
a structured home exercise program. The mechanism of injury, a rear impact with forward and rebound loading of the lower
extremity, is consistent with the type of knee trauma described. Early visits were more frequent, and the frequency of visits
decreased steadily as symptoms improved and strength and mobility returned. Examination findings include localized tenderness
and a positive effusion sign along the medial joint line, which support the reported injury. Other ligamentous and neurovascular
tests were within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving this knee, and no earlier recrods were
identified that would suggest a pre-existing condition. Billing records were reviewed and reflect no duplicate or repeated charges
for the same services. At discharge, the patient was improving with residual mild stiffness and was released to independent
exercise with follow-up as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
